summary: Fasting glucose is the amount of sugar in your blood after not eating for at least eight hours. It is a snapshot of a single moment, which is why it is usually read alongside HbA1c rather than on its own.
what_it_measures: The concentration of glucose in blood plasma after an overnight fast, reported in mmol/L.

interpretations.meaning: A raised fasting glucose suggests your body is not clearing sugar from the blood efficiently. 5.6-6.9 mmol/L suggests impaired fasting glucose; 7.0 mmol/L or above on two occasions is consistent with diabetes.
A low fasting glucose means blood sugar has fallen further than expected. In people not on diabetes medication this is uncommon and usually needs explaining.

when_to_seek_help: If your fasting glucose is 7.0 mmol/L or above, or you feel shaky, sweaty or confused when you have not eaten, contact your GP.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
